subject: Unconventional library loading with apply will not work for deployment (package not found)

messages.author: 0d02793ea1b36c86
messages.subject: Unconventional library loading with apply will not work for deployment (package not found)
parts:
Hi.

I just thought I'd make a post here, even though it is not a question, but in case other have similar issues in the future.

I have, lately, taken to loading multiple packages using sapply.

example:
> LIBS=c("rio","rmarkdown","tidyverse","plotly","png","svglite")
> sapply(LIBS, library, character.only=T)

Of course, this works perfectly locally, but not when deploying the app to shinyapp.io. When initiating on the server, it would throw errors about the packages not being installed. It tok me so long to understand what was going on, initially thinking I had not installed the packages in the "correct" way, and was going round in circles trying to fix the issue.

In the end, I found this post: https://github.com/rstudio/rsconnect/issues/88
and understood what was going on. I had not understood the search the deployment does to find the packages necessary for the app to run. Since it specifically searches for string calls to library() or require(), wrapping them in an apply obviously would not provide any results.

so, in case other have started loading libraries in this new an peculiar way: it wont work for your shinyApp deployment!

messages.author: 26b647b408a2e02e
messages.subject: Re: Unconventional library loading with apply will not work for deployment (package not found)
parts:
There are some articles about dependency packages for shiny server that explained the requirement.

I've been using pacman because I want my app to install missing packages automatically in local mode. Usually you must install all the packages before running the app, with pacman you can run the app, and the packages will be installed if missing. 

So I have

if (!require("pacman")) install.packages("pacman")
pacman::p_load(shiny, shinydashboard, DT,
               markdown, crayon, rmarkdown, knitr,
               ctmm, data.table, parallel,
               ggplot2, scales, grid, gridExtra, lubridate,
               httr, stringr, XML, xml2, zip)


Imagine how many library calls I need for this, and how many libraries I need to ask user to install before running the app...

The pacman usage doesn't work in shinyapps.io for similar reasons. I created a PR for packrat (which is the underlying mechanism used by shinyapps.io) to support the usage, but they don't want to merge it as official.

If this feature (or install missing packages automatically) is useful for you, you can download my fork, install the package locally, then you can use pacman in your app.
